newsitem.title: UK: Laura Ashley hits 2-year low, sterling cited.
newsitem.headline: Laura Ashley hits 2-year low, sterling cited.

text.p: Shares in Laura Ashley Holdings Plc fell more than seven percent on Thursday, missing out on a retail sector rally amid fears over its exposure to strong sterling, analysts and traders said.
The share drop was also blamed on rumours that one trader was an aggressive seller this week and on talk that analysts were getting ready to lower their earnings estimates for the year.
By 1502 GMT, the stock traded 5p lower at 63-1/2p, its weakest price since March 1995 and well off its 1997 high of 170p.

Investors were shopping for British retail stocks whose earnings were concentrated domestically, as opposed to Laura Ashley, which was already hammered in the last three months by the departure of two executives and a profits warning.
"Laura Ashley has an overseas content, while people are buying in the sector with a domestic focus," one analyst said. "People just gave up on the stock some months ago."
Retailers Kingfisher Plc, Dixons Group Plc, Storehouse Plc and Argos Plc all posted strong gains on Thursday.
